Highest-trust: the deploy wizard's root-password field ("Generate" + copy promising it's "shown on your server page") was never submitted and the worker ALWAYS generates its own — a customer's typed/generated password was silently discarded; UI made honest. Four forms wiped typed input on rejected submit (incl. a pasted DKIM/SPF TXT and a new password). Plus dead-ends and a11y/mobile.

Update the "Known gaps — the honest inventory" section (add these to the Fixed table, re-check the "Still not true" list against them, correct any citation the commits moved), and any chapter these make wrong (billing/renewal, admin metrics, mail, migration, auth). Three findings from the mail-platform audit.

smtp_pass was the last secret in the Setting table stored as PLAINTEXT,
while mailbox passwords and the Cloudflare token both use the AES-256-GCM

at-rest exposure — a database or backup leak hands out the SMTP relay

(lib/actions-settings.ts) and decrypted on read (lib/mailer.ts), the read
tolerating a legacy plaintext row (decryptSecret returns null on a value
that is not iv:tag:ciphertext, so it falls through to the raw value) so
nothing breaks until an operator next saves the settings.

NotificationPrefs told the customer "Payment receipts are still always
sent today." That became false when lib/stripe.ts started passing
kind:"receipt" and lib/prefs.ts tiered receipt as ACCOUNT — so turning off
"Account email" now DOES stop receipts. The note and the file's own
docblock (which claimed "the receipt send site is still ungated") both now
match the behaviour, and say plainly that critical notices like suspension
are never suppressible.

before the session limit killed it, despite its final transcript line):
worker/restore.ts reapplyIdentity re-applies the Server row's network/size
after qmrestore --force AND reads it back, throwing (VM left stopped) on
any mismatch — closing the "restored VM boots on another customer's IP"
hole; and worker/game-config.ts now quotes `-P '${shq(port)}'`.

bite. 539 total, tsc clean, build clean, deployed.

Mail: a Mailcow refusal is not an outage — stop deleting live mailboxes

removeMailbox and setMailboxSuspended wrapped every Mailcow call in
`.catch(() => {})`, then wrote the database and returned ok:true. Mailcow
answers HTTP 200 even on logical failure (signalling via a type:"danger"
payload), and its client already surfaces that as a MailcowError — but the
swallow threw it away.

Consequence on removeMailbox, which IS wired to the Remove button: when
Mailcow REFUSED the delete (reachable, mailbox still present), our row was
deleted anyway and the customer was told it was gone — leaving a LIVE
mailbox still receiving their mail, with no record of it in the product.
Silent data loss.

The fix distinguishes the two failure modes, because they demand opposite
actions:
  - REFUSED (reachable, returned an error): the mail server and our DB
    disagree. Return the error and KEEP the row — never delete our only
    record of a mailbox that still exists.
  - UNREACHABLE (transport failure): the server may just be down. Proceed,
    but tell the customer plainly the mailbox may still exist and to retry.

lib/mailcow.ts: MailcowError now carries a MAILCOW_UNREACHABLE sentinel
set only in the fetch() catch, with an `unreachable` getter and an
`isMailcowUnreachable(e)` guard. A negative status that can never collide
with a real HTTP code.

setMailboxSuspended got the same treatment: a refusal no longer lets us
write a SUSPENDED/ACTIVE status the mail server rejected — a "suspended"
mailbox that keeps delivering is its own lie.

(a success-with-a-caveat, not a red error), via a new `notice` channel
distinct from `error`.

suite red). 537 total, tsc clean, build clean, deployed and smoke-tested.

4096	# Part VI — Honest status
4097	
4098	## The recurring defect — reporting an outcome nobody verified
4099	
4100	**This codebase has one bug, and it has shipped many times.** A surface reports an outcome it never
4101	verified. Every variant below is the same shape:
4102	
4103	```
4104	 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
4105	 │  do something  ──►  ASSUME it worked  ──►  write success             │
4106	 │                                            notify the customer       │
4107	 │                                            render it as fact         │
4108	 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
4109	                    ▲
4110	                    └── the missing step: ASK THE WORLD WHETHER IT WORKED
4111	```
4112	
4113	Five instances found on a single day:
4114	
4115	| Instance | What was claimed | What was true |
4116	|---|---|---|
4117	| SSL | Certificate rows `ACTIVE` with a `now + 90d` expiry and *"Your Let's Encrypt certificate is active"* | No certbot ran. No certificate existed anywhere on the box |
4118	| Game settings | *"Game settings applied on `<hostname>`"* | Nothing was written to the VM; the `(sandbox)` qualifier was suppressed because `SANDBOX` is false in production |
4119	| Migration | `Sites actually serving: 4/4` | Six of the customer's domains were dark. The denominator was "domains we chose to publish", so the metric was 100% **by construction** |
4120	| Domain markup | Admin panel displayed **0%** | Customers were charged **25%**. Nothing read the setting at all |
4121	| Auto-suspend kill switch | An admin toggle that appeared to be saved | It was saved, and read by nothing |
4122	
4123	**The six shapes to watch for**, because they recur:
4124	
4125	1. **Simulated-success fall-through.** A feature flag is unset, so the code takes a branch that writes
4126	   the success value without doing the work.
4127	2. **Saved-but-unread.** An admin sets a value; nothing consumes it. Worse when a panel *states* what
4128	   it affects.
4129	3. **Env-vs-setting split.** The value is read from `process.env` while the admin edits a `Setting`
4130	   row (or vice versa). Both the domain markup and `referral_reward_cents` were this; both are now
4131	   closed and no instance is known to survive.
4132	4. **A metric that cannot fail.** A denominator chosen from the numerator's own set; a shell command
4133	   ending `; true`; a status written outside the `if` that decided it.
4134	5. **A second definition of something that already had one.** The newest shape, and the one that did
4135	   the most damage in the last two days: a renewal price computed twice, a promo basis computed twice,
4136	   a `lastAutoBackup` written in two places, an address lowercased in three. It reads as diligence and
4137	   behaves as drift, and **it is usually introduced by the fix for the previous bug** — the game-server
4138	   overcharge was created by the patch for the "+30 days" overcharge, hours later, by the same hand.
4139	   The remedy is never "make the two agree"; it is to delete one and make the survivor the only caller.
4140	6. **A guard whose comment describes the only way a thing can happen.** The deploy wizard's Enter-key
4141	   guard asserted in its own comment that *"Deploy only ever happens via the explicit button"* — and
4142	   that sentence is precisely why nobody looked for the other way, which was React swapping the
4143	   button's `type` mid-click. A comment is not an invariant. Put the claim where it can fail.
4144	
4145	**Three things this project got right, and they are the patterns to copy:**
4146	
4147	- **Fail loudly instead of simulating.** `worker/ssl.ts:699`, `worker/game-config.ts:86`,
4148	  `worker/websites.ts:157-162` and `worker/databases.ts:159-165` now *throw* with an explanation naming
4149	  the flag, rather than writing a success. The customer sees a failure with a real reason. That is
4150	  strictly better than a comforting lie, even though it means the feature is visibly unavailable.
4151	- **Delete the control you cannot enforce.** `Membership.areas` was written, echoed back as saved, and
4152	  read by nothing. Rather than leave it, the control was **removed** and the customer is told what a
4153	  membership actually grants (`lib/actions-teams.ts:19-21`).
4154	- **Make the promise true rather than walking back the copy.** The migration report was rewritten to
4155	  promise *"Nxeon issues the certificate automatically within about 30 minutes"* — which was false the
4156	  moment it shipped. The answer was `postCutoverTlsSweep`, not a smaller promise. **A promise the
4157	  product does not keep is the same defect as a success it did not verify**, and it is fixable in
4158	  either direction; prefer the direction that leaves the customer better off.
4159	
4160	And the meta-lesson, from `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md:115-127`, about failure #25 recurring four
4161	months after it was written up as #13 in the same file:
4162	
4163	> **A documented fix is not a fix. Nothing in the engine read this file.** … a failure mode that has
4164	> been observed twice belongs in code, and a field note describing a fix nobody implemented is worth
4165	> approximately nothing.
4166	
4167	Which is why **this manual is not a substitute for a check**. If you find yourself documenting a
4168	behaviour rather than asserting it, ask whether a test or a guard would be a better place to put the
4169	sentence.
4170	
4171	## Known gaps — the honest inventory
4172	
4173	Every entry below was re-opened and re-checked against the tree on **2026-07-27 at commit `2d8fedd`**,
4174	seven commits after the previous pass. **Nearly every line number in this chapter moved** — `lib/actions.ts`,
4175	`lib/stripe.ts`, `worker/billing.ts`, `worker/migrate.ts` and `worker/migrate-real.ts` all changed
4176	substantially, and `3aa24d7` alone touched 76 files. Several agents edit this repo concurrently, so
4177	this will happen again. **When a citation misses, grep the quoted symbol rather than assuming the
4178	claim is stale — and correct the number here when you do.** A line number in this document is "this
4179	function, roughly here"; the symbol is the real citation. Classification:
4180	
4181	- **WORKS** — verified end to end.
4182	- **SIMULATED** — produces a fabricated result.
4183	- **UNVERIFIED SUCCESS** — does real work but reports success without checking it.
4184	- **SAVED-BUT-UNREAD** — written by a UI, consumed by nothing.
4185	- **DEAD** — implemented, never called.
4186	- **PARTIAL** — real but incomplete or overstated.
